intervals.label: TAIGA construction
intervals.note: Start: "In 2012 in the frame of Russian-German joint research activities, the construction of two new detectors was started." (Kostunin et al., arXiv:1903.07460, Section 2).
intervals.quote: In 2022, we completed the deployment and commissioning of the TAIGA-1 hybrid complex

intervals.label: TAIGA operation
intervals.note: 2013 is the year the first TAIGA-type array, Tunka-HiSCORE (later TAIGA-HiSCORE), went into operation; the Tunka-133 array had been taking data since 2009. The first IACT was deployed in 2017 and the second in 2018. The most recent statement read (2022) describes TAIGA-1 as complete and in operation.
intervals.quote: was put into operation one year later, in 2013

placements.quote: in the Tunka valley 50 km to the west from Lake Baikal (51.49 N, 103.04 E)

station_count.quote: It consists of 120 TAIGA-HiSCORE wide-angle Cherenkov stations

telescope_count.quote: three 4-m class Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACT)

description.quote: a low-threshold non-imaging air-Cherenkov array originally called Tunka-HiSCORE
description.value: A low-threshold non-imaging air-Cherenkov timing array, put into operation in 2013.

description.quote: a digital radio array called Tunka Radio Extension (Tunka-Rex)
description.value: A digital radio antenna array for air-shower radio emission, deployed and commissioned in 2012.

description.quote: the former KASCADEGrande scintillators were shipped to Tunka and formed the Tunka-Grande array
description.value: Scintillator array formed from former KASCADE-Grande scintillators shipped to Tunka in 2014-2015.

summary.plain: A hybrid of light stations, imaging telescopes, radio antennas and particle counters in one valley, for PeV gamma rays and cosmic rays.
summary.technical: TAIGA-1: 120 HiSCORE stations (1 km2), three IACTs (about 9.6 degree field of view), Tunka-Grande and TAIGA-MUON scintillators (250 m2), Tunka-Rex radio array, and the older Tunka-133 Cherenkov array.

technology.quote: It consists of 120 TAIGA-HiSCORE wide-angle Cherenkov stations, three 4-m class Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACT) and 250 m2 of scintillation particle detectors
technology.value: Hybrid of a wide-angle Cherenkov timing array (HiSCORE), imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes and scintillator arrays.
